title: The Archive of New Lagos
premise: Marguerite Montrose arrives in New Lagos to investigate a string of 'impossible' insurance claims and discovers the colony's reactor is failing on a hidden countdown, its records falsified for decades. As the colony's children begin sharing one recurring dream — of the cryobay where half the founding population still sleeps — Marguerite realizes her own missing memories are woven into it: she was born here, and her mother chose who would sleep. The dream is the sleeping minds' plea to wake before the power runs out, but the reactor can only sustain one half of humanity. In the end, Marguerite breaks the archive open, exposes the founders' original lottery as rigged against the poor, and chooses to wake the sleepers while the waking colonists enter a shared cold-sleep rotation — splitting the burden so no half of humanity is abandoned.
about_author: Vesper Blackwood is the pen name of a former marine insurance adjuster who spent seven years documenting failed settlements along the West African orbital corridor before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about bureaucracy, memory, and the paperwork of apocalypse from a houseboat in Lagos Lagoon.

chapters.title: The Claim That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. An insurance investigator lands in New Lagos to assess a death claim for a man officially dead eleven years prior. The colony is beautiful, quiet, and strangely uncurious about her arrival. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack as she notices no one asks why she's really here.

chapters.title: Ledgers Written in Two Hands
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. In the colonial archive she finds maintenance logs alternating between two handwriting styles across forty years — as if someone periodically rewrote history. The reactor output figures are suspiciously flat. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt, undercut by the sense that the archive wants to be found.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. At a school inspection tied to a claim, six children independently describe an identical dream: a blue-lit hall, rows of glass coffins, a woman counting them aloud. Their teacher dismisses it; Marguerite does not. Emotional beat: unease deepening into recognition — she has had the dream too.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Counts
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. She sketches the dream's counting woman from memory and freezes: the face is her own mother's, whom she buried on Earth at age nine. Her employer's file lists her birthplace as Earth. It is wrong. Emotional beat: vertigo — the investigation turns inward.

chapters.title: Interview with the Undertaker
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The colony's aging mortician confirms the impossible claimant was cremated twice, decades apart, and lets slip that the first body came 'from downstairs' — the sealed sublevel beneath the reactor. Emotional beat: grief-tinged complicity; he has kept the secret out of love, not malice.

chapters.title: Downstairs
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Bribing her way past a caretaker, she enters the sublevel: a functioning cryobay holding four hundred sleepers, including a woman whose face matches her mother at thirty. A countdown terminal reads 214 days. Emotional beat: awe collapsing into dread — the dream is a broadcast from the dying.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Owes
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Cross-referencing power budgets, she proves the colony has been quietly cannibalizing the cryobay's reserves for thirty years. Every comfort above ground is stolen from the sleepers below. Emotional beat: moral nausea — everyone she's met is both victim and thief.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Tea
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Mayor Adeyemi receives her with warm hospitality and colder arithmetic: waking four hundred people now means rationing, hardship, maybe death for those already awake. He offers her a bribe and a ticket home. Emotional beat: temptation — the easy exit, beautifully wrapped.

chapters.title: Marguerite Montrose, Age Zero
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. In the restricted births registry she finds her own record: born in New Lagos, cryo-listed at infancy, extracted illegally by her mother during the last lottery. Her Earth childhood was a forged life. Emotional beat: identity shattering — she is evidence of the crime she's investigating.

chapters.title: The Lottery Papers
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The original selection documents reveal the 'random' lottery was weighted: the poor, the sick, and the politically inconvenient were put under. Her mother, an archive clerk, smuggled out one infant — her. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Dream Logic
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The shared dream intensifies colony-wide; adults begin dreaming it too. Inside it, the counting woman speaks directly to Marguerite, reciting names and dates — a message encoded in memory. Emotional beat: surrender — she stops treating the dream as symptom and starts treating it as testimony.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Days
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. She presents her findings to the colony council; the room splits between denial, rage, and a young engineer, Tomi, who verifies the countdown independently. Sabotage of her hotel room follows that night. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve — the truth now has enemies.

chapters.title: Tomi's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Tomi. The engineer walks Marguerite through the brutal math: full wake-up exceeds capacity; doing nothing kills all sleepers. But staggered rotational cold-sleep — cycling wakes and sleeps in shifts — might work if the waking generation consents to share the burden. Emotional beat: fragile hope built on sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Town Meeting
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Before three hundred colonists, she plays the archive's falsification trail end to end. Old families deny; the children, uncannily, recite the sleepers' names from their dreams, making the abstract dead suddenly personal. Emotional beat: collective reckoning — grief displacing defensiveness.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Dream
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The whole colony dreams the cryobay simultaneously; in the morning, the vote for rotational waking passes by nine votes. The mayor concedes but warns that whoever controls the thaw sequence controls the future. Emotional beat: exhausted victory shadowed by coming conflict.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: POV Tomi. Someone floods the cryobay's coolant lines; forty sleepers die before emergency freezing. Tomi traces the sabotage to the mayor's faction and to a second, hidden countdown accelerating the crisis. Emotional beat: fury and mourning — the cost of hesitation made flesh.

chapters.title: The Counting Woman Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Against protocol, she initiates an early thaw of one sleeper: her mother, alive, middle-aged, remembering everything. Their reunion is not tender — her mother defends the lottery as triage that saved the colony. Emotional beat: the confrontation she has dreaded since chapter four.

chapters.title: Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Her mother hands over the true master ledger: the founders' full reasoning, the bribes, the bodies, and a final entry naming Marguerite as designated arbiter — written before Marguerite was born. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of an inheritance chosen for you.

chapters.title: The Countdown Vote
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. With 40 days left, the colony must ratify rotational cold-sleep or choose which half lives. Marguerite refuses to be the arbiter her mother designed and puts the choice to an open assembly, using the children's dream-names to read the sleepers into the record as citizens. Emotional beat: climax — authorship reclaimed through refusal of inherited power.

chapters.title: First Thaw
chapters.summary: POV Tomi. The first shift-cycle begins: two hundred sleepers wake to a colony that has learned their names; two hundred colonists say goodbye and lie down voluntarily. The mayor's faction, broken by the sabotage scandal, stands down. Emotional beat: bittersweet ceremony — grief and hope in the same breath.

chapters.title: Amending the Archive
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. She rewrites the colonial archive in her own hand, appending every falsification, every name, her mother's confession, and her own true birth record — then files her final insurance report declaring New Lagos insolvent in trust and solvent in people. Emotional beat: quiet catharsis — memory restored as public property.

chapters.title: The Second Dream
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Months later, the shared dream returns transformed: the blue hall bright, the coffins empty, the counting woman smiling and off-duty. Marguerite, staying on as the colony's archivist, finally dreams of nothing but tomorrow. Emotional beat: resolution — identity rebuilt not from what was hidden, but what is now honestly kept.
